title: [Feature][KV Pool] Support Mooncake SSD prefetch on exist
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds optional Mooncake SSD-to-DRAM prefetch on exist queries. When `enable_ssd_prefetch=true` in `mooncake.json`, `batch_is_exist` passes `ExistOptions(prefetch_to_memory=True)`, so Mooncake promotes SSD-only objects into DRAM during the cache probe, and a follow-up get is served from DRAM instead of SSD. Feature design lives in the Mooncake PR (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4272); concept from kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2213.

- Parse `enable_ssd_prefetch`, `ssd_prefetch_cooldown_sec`, and `ssd_prefetch_dedup_ttl_sec`; forward each throttle knob to `store.setup()` only when explicitly set, so omitted fields keep Mooncake defaults (5s backoff, 30s dedup TTL).
- Capability probes keep this safe on older Mooncake builds: without `ExistOptions`, prefetch is disabled with a warning instead of failing initialization.
- When a knob is forwarded, setup uses the config-dict overload; the store then owns its TransferEngine instead of sharing the global one.
- Document the new `mooncake.json` fields in the kv-pool feature guide.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. New optional `mooncake.json` fields (`enable_ssd_prefetch`, `ssd_prefetch_cooldown_sec`, `ssd_prefetch_dedup_ttl_sec`). Behavior changes only when `enable_ssd_prefetch=true` and a compatible Mooncake build is installed; everything is off by default.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests (148 pass):

    pytest -sv tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_backend.py

Covers config parsing (defaults / set / null), capability probes, prefetch resolve logic, both setup paths (keyword vs config-dict and the TransferEngine ownership that follows), and the `exists()` call path with and without prefetch options.

End-to-end on Ascend A2 with the Mooncake PR head: TTFT A/B and SSD-offload smoke, evidence in the Mooncake PR.
